It's a bleak book yes; a hard-hitting Southern piece of fiction that makes you want to take a shower, and that has a story that likes to meander, but it did produce a few laughs; most prominently and memorably being when the 'moonlight melonmounter' is mentioned - that being Suttree's friend, Gene, who got caught in a farmer's field shagging a pulpy fruit and sent to the work farm. I much preferred this to anything by the likes of Faulkner or O'Connor as it simply got its hooks into me and wouldn't let go. 4.5/5 ... Cormac McCarthy at his best--..writing with the throttle wide open--is still the closest thing to heroin you can buy in a bookstore.
